title: The depth of a module is at most dim(R/p) for every associated prime p
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) and let $M$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal for which there is an element $z\in M$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\{a\in R: az=0\}=\mathfrak p$ (an associated prime of $M$). Then $\dim(R/\mathfrak p)\ge\operatorname{depth}(M)$, where $\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$ is the Krull dimension of the ring $R/\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ is the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth].

proof.text:
(If $\mathfrak m$ is associated, the depth is $0$.) Let $N$ be a finite $R$-module with $\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Ass}(N)$: some $z\in N$ has $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\mathfrak m$, so $z
eq0$ and $fz=0$ for every $f\in\mathfrak m$. Then no $N$-regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_r$ in $\mathfrak m$ has $r\ge1$: condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $i=1$ asks that multiplication by $f_1$ on $N/0\cdot N=N$ be injective, but $f_1z=0=f_1\cdot0$ with $z
eq0$. The empty sequence is $N$-regular since $N
eq0$. By Step 1, $\operatorname{depth}(N)=0$. In particular for $N=M$ and $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)$: if $\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)$ then $\operatorname{depth}(M)=0\le\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$, the latter being $\ge0$ because $R/\mathfrak p$ is a nonzero ring (it has the prime ideal $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p$, a chain of length $0$ in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]).

proof.text: (The depth is a finite integer, and the induction.) Let $N$ be a finite $R$-module with $\operatorname{Ass}(N)\neq\emptyset$. If $\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Ass}(N)$, then $\operatorname{depth}(N)=0$ by Step 2. Otherwise [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] gives $x\in\mathfrak m$ which is a nonzerodivisor on $N$, and since $N\neq0$ (Step 1) [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one] says that $\operatorname{depth}(N)$ is a finite integer $\ge1$. So $\operatorname{depth}(N)\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ in all cases. For an integer $d\ge0$ let $Q(d)$ be the claim: for every finite $R$-module $N$ and every $\mathfrak p'\in\operatorname{Ass}(N)$ with $\operatorname{depth}(N)=d$ one has $\dim(R/\mathfrak p')\ge d$. The lemma is $Q(\operatorname{depth}(M))$ for $N=M$ (if $\operatorname{Ass}(M)=\emptyset$ there is nothing to prove). We prove $Q(d)$ by induction on $d$. Base $d=0$: $\dim(R/\mathfrak p')\ge0$ as in Step 2. In Steps 4-7 let $d\ge1$, assume $Q(d-1)$, and let $N$ be finite, $\mathfrak p'=:\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(N)$, $\operatorname{depth}(N)=d$. (The source proves the case $d=1$ separately and inducts from $d>1$; the argument of Steps 4-7 covers $d=1$ as well, the inductive hypothesis $Q(0)$ being the base case.)

proof.text: (The dimension drops by one: $\dim R/(\mathfrak p+(x))=\dim(R/\mathfrak p)-1$.) Put $\bar R=R/\mathfrak p$. It is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (its ideals are the images of the ideals of $R$ containing $\mathfrak p$, so an ascending chain of them lifts to one in $R$) and local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p$ (its maximal ideals are the images of the maximal ideals of $R$ containing $\mathfrak p$); it is a domain since $\mathfrak p$ is prime. The image $\bar x$ of $x$ lies in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p$ and is nonzero by Step 4, hence is a nonzerodivisor of the domain $\bar R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension] $\dim\bar R$ is a finite integer, and by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] (Tag 00KW) $\dim(\bar R/\bar x\bar R)+1=\dim\bar R$. Let $A=R/(\mathfrak p+(x))$; the surjection $R\to\bar R/\bar x\bar R$ has kernel $\mathfrak p+(x)$, so $A\cong\bar R/\bar x\bar R$ and $e:=\dim A=\dim(R/\mathfrak p)-1$, a finite integer. As $x\in\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak p+(x)\subseteq\mathfrak m\neq R$, so $A\neq0$ and $e\ge0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BK4 (lemma-depth-dim-associated-primes, line 17985), proof lines 17991-18020, third paragraph: 'By Lemma 00KW we have dim(R/p + (x)) = dim(R/p) - 1'

proof.text: (The omitted small argument: a prime $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $\mathfrak p+(x)$ with $\dim(R/\mathfrak q)=\dim(R/\mathfrak p)-1$.) The prime ideals of $A=R/(\mathfrak p+(x))$ are the $\mathfrak Q/(\mathfrak p+(x))$ with $\mathfrak Q\supseteq\mathfrak p+(x)$ a prime of $R$, inclusions preserved both ways; so the minimal prime ideals of $A$ are the images of the primes of $R$ minimal over $\mathfrak p+(x)$, and for such a prime $\mathfrak q$ one has $A/(\mathfrak q/(\mathfrak p+(x)))\cong R/\mathfrak q$. Since $e=\dim A$ is a finite integer $\ge0$ (Step 5) there is a chain $Q_0\subsetneq Q_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Q_e$ of primes of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] (with $I=0$ in $A$) there is a minimal prime $Q'\subseteq Q_0$ of $A$; then $Q'\subsetneq Q_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Q_e$ (for $e=0$: just $Q'$) is a chain of length $e$ of primes of $A$ containing $Q'$, whose images form a chain of length $e$ in $A/Q'$; so $\dim(A/Q')\ge e$. Conversely the primes of $A/Q'$ are the images of the primes of $A$ containing $Q'$, so a chain in $A/Q'$ gives one of the same length in $A$, and $\dim(A/Q')\le\dim A=e$. Let $\mathfrak q\subset R$ be the inverse image of $Q'$: a prime of $R$ minimal over $\mathfrak p+(x)$, with $R/\mathfrak q\cong A/Q'$, hence $\dim(R/\mathfrak q)=e=\dim(R/\mathfrak p)-1$. (This is the hint of the source: the dimension of the Noetherian local ring $A$ is the maximum of $\dim A/\mathfrak r$ over its minimal primes $\mathfrak r$.)

proof.text: (Passing to $N/x^nN$ and concluding.) By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-prime-power-quotient] (Tag 0CN5) applied to $N$, $x\in\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(N)$ and $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $\mathfrak p+(x)$ (Step 6), there is $n\ge1$ with $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}(N/x^nN)$. The element $x^n\in\mathfrak m$ is a nonzerodivisor on $N$ (multiplication by $x^n$ is the $n$-fold composite of the injective multiplication by $x$), and $N\neq0$ (Step 1), so by [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one] applied to $x^n$: $\operatorname{depth}(N/x^nN)=\operatorname{depth}(N)-1=d-1$. $N/x^nN$ is a finite $R$-module (a quotient of $N$). By the inductive hypothesis $Q(d-1)$ applied to $N/x^nN$ and $\mathfrak q$: $\dim(R/\mathfrak q)\ge d-1$. With Step 6, $\dim(R/\mathfrak p)=\dim(R/\mathfrak q)+1\ge d$. This proves $Q(d)$, hence $Q(d)$ for all $d\ge0$, and with Step 3 the lemma: $\dim(R/\mathfrak p)\ge\operatorname{depth}(M)$ for every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}(M)$.
